Overview

A product that worked but leaked recruiters at every step

ManyJobs is a recruiter-side hiring platform for entry-level Sales, Service, and Manufacturing roles in Tamil Nadu. The product was functionally complete — you could register, post a job, and manage applications — but the journey was riddled with friction that caused early abandonment at almost every stage.

I ran a competitive benchmark across 8 platforms, then a heuristic evaluation and cognitive walkthrough of the full funnel. The result: 20 distinct problems across 5 stages, triaged by severity (P0/P1/P2), with redesigned screens for each.

Competitive context

The benchmark that set the target

Before touching any screen, I mapped ManyJobs against 8 competitors on three axes: price, onboarding speed, and simplicity. This gave every recommendation a named, checkable external bar — not a vague "make it better."

PlatformPrice to startOnboarding speedKey gap vs ManyJobs
ManyJobs (redesigned)₹0~3 min targetRegional TN expertise + WhatsApp-first
Naukri Recruit₹999/month~30 min slowManyJobs wins on price + speed
Indeed HireFree but sponsorship required~15 minNo regional/language depth
JobHai₹0~3 min matchedPan-India, no Tamil Nadu focus
Hirist₹0~2 min matchedTech-only, no Sales/Service/Mfg
LinkedIn Talent$4000+/month~45 min slowManyJobs is the SME alternative
Apna₹0InstantUnstructured, no candidate verification
Unstop₹500+~10 minCampus/intern-only, not SME

The gap: ManyJobs was priced right but onboarding speed was losing to JobHai and Hirist. The redesign target was clear — match their 3-minute flow, while keeping the two things no competitor had: Tamil Nadu regional depth and WhatsApp-first communication.

Problems & redesign — screen by screen

20 problems across 5 stages, fully fixed

Stage 1 — Landing page

LIVE DESIGN (Figma)
Before
REDESIGN (Prototype)
After
P0
Headline is candidate-facing copy on a recruiter product. "Entry level Sales, Service and Manufacturing jobs" describes job categories, not recruiter value. Cold visitors assume it's a job board for seekers.
P1
Registration form appears before value is established. Asking for phone number before any proof is shown violates the value→action sequence. Cognitive friction: "What am I signing up for?"
P0
Pricing completely hidden. No pricing section on the landing page. Recruiters only discover ₹499–₹19,999 tiers after registration — after the FAQ told them it was free.
P1
Generic feature cards, no outcome language. "Candidates can contact you directly" instead of "Get applications in 2–4 hours." No proof points tied to features.
FIX
New headline: "Hire entry-level talent in 48 hours. No fees to start." Backed by 410,000+ candidates, 50,000+ companies, 2–4hr median response. Pricing table added before any CTA. Value props rewritten as outcomes with metrics.

Pricing section (new — didn't exist before)

NEWTransparent before signup3-tierResolves FAQ contradiction
FIX
Full pricing visible before account creation. Free tier / Starter ₹499 / Professional ₹999 — stated explicitly with what each includes, including what happens after your first 100 credits run out. The FAQ was also rewritten to match exactly, eliminating the "it's free" vs "pay to continue" contradiction.

FAQ — the P0 trust break fixed

LIVE — FAQ says "no charges"
Before
REDESIGN — Full credit model stated
After
P0
Business-model contradiction. FAQ answer: "No, currently there are no charges." Dashboard reality: "You need ₹499–₹19,999 to post more jobs." The moment a recruiter discovers this after registering, trust is broken — they switch to Naukri.
FIX
FAQ rewritten with full transparency: Free tier (100 credits), Starter ₹499/mo (100 credits), Professional ₹999/mo (unlimited). "Anyone can start for free — you only pay when you want more volume than the free tier covers."

Stage 2 — Phone entry

Step 1 of 2 indicatorOTP hint visible upfrontNo blame language
FIX
Step context added. "Step 1 of 2 · Create account" visible at top — user knows exactly where they are. Progress bar added. OTP hint ("OTP will be sent") visible before submission.

OTP — normal state and error state

LIVE — Blame error message
Before
REDESIGN — Neutral framing + timer
After
P1
"Entered OTP is wrong. Please check and enter again." Blame language makes the user feel at fault. No timer, no expiry context, no recovery guidance beyond the message itself.
FIX
Changed to: "That code didn't match" — neutral, not blaming. Added: expiry countdown timer, two resend paths (SMS + WhatsApp), auto-focus on retry. Error uses icon + text (not color alone — accessibility fix).

Stage 3 — Verification (3-step with context)

LIVE — "You can only post after verified"
Before
REDESIGN — Why, how long, 95% instant
After
P0
Gate with no explanation. "You can post jobs only after you're verified" — no reason WHY, no timeline, no proof it's quick. Feels like punishment, not protection.
FIX
Context-first gate: States why (fraud prevention, candidate trust), how long (2–3 minutes), proof (95% verified instantly). 3-step progress bar visible throughout. Each form field has a help text explaining what to enter and why.
Step 2
Success
P1
Success screen used wrong brand name: "You have successfully created your Jobzapp recruiter account." Fixed to ManyJobs. Now shows all verified items (phone ✓, company ✓), confirms 100 credits added, and gives one clear next action.

Stage 4 — Job posting: 1 long form → 3-step wizard

The original form had 15+ fields — text inputs, dropdowns, button groups, conditional fields — all on one page with zero progress feedback. Estimated abandonment: 40–50%. Each step below = one third of that old form, isolated for focus.

Step 1 — Job basics
Step 2 — Job details
FIX
Step 1 — Job basics: Title (with autocomplete suggestions), combined Category + Work Type selector (was 2 separate fields), location, openings. Progress bar shows 33%. Save draft button always visible.
FIX
Step 2 — Job details: Description with character counter, employment type, urgency, salary — now optional with "discuss with candidate" fallback. Progress bar shows 66%. Salary dropdowns replace blank text fields.
Step 3 — Interview prefs
Review before posting
FIX
Step 3 — Interview prefs: Interview method (walk-in fields only appear conditionally), contact details. "Decide after reviewing" option added — reduces pressure. 100% progress bar.
FIX
Review screen (new): Shows all three steps summarised with edit links. Shows exact credit cost (1 credit) and remaining balance (99) before the irreversible "Post" action. Sets expectation: "Usually approved in 2–4 hours."

Stage 5 — Post-job success and dashboard

Job posted — success state
Dashboard
P0
No post-job success state existed in the original design. After posting, users were left to guess what happens next — no confirmation, no next action.
FIX
Rich success screen: Confirms job title + location, shows review timeline (2–4 hours), three explicit next actions — Share on WhatsApp, View Dashboard, Post Another Job. Credit balance updated immediately.
FIX
Dashboard: All posted jobs visible with status badges, applicant counts, credit balance in header. Edit and view actions per job. Post another job CTA prominent.
Impact

Projected improvement across every stage

Funnel stageBefore (audit estimate)After (projected)
Landing → registration~75%~90%
Registration → first job posted~50%~85%
End-to-end completion~37%~65–76%
Time to post a job~30 min~3 min
Business model trust (FAQ)Contradicted pricingFully transparent pre-signup
Competitive positioningSlower than JobHai/HiristMatched on onboarding speed

Audit-stage projections based on funnel friction analysis — not live A/B results. Next phase: 5-user moderated usability testing + A/B on hero headline.

The most severe problem in the funnel was a business-communication problem, not a form-design problem.

The FAQ/pricing contradiction (P0) would have undermined any amount of polish downstream — it broke trust at the exact moment a recruiter had to decide whether to continue. Fixing copy and the information architecture mattered more than visual refinement here.
